newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank Melb booms as rumours revived.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank Melb booms as rumours revived.

text.p: Shares in Victorian-based regional bank, Bank of Melbourne Ltd, climbed 4.7 percent to an eight week high of A$9.00 on Thursday as long-running speculation stirred again that the bank was a takeover target.

While brokers were unconvinced the resignation of chief executive officer David Airey made a takeover more likely, they suggested his departure had focussed attention on upcoming release at the end of March of the Wallis inquiry in the finance sector.
"I don't think Airey's leaving necessarily makes it more vulnerable but Wallis is due to report in a few weeks and we may see some more action then," said a Sydney broker.
Rationalisation of the banking sector is widely expected after inquiry chairman Stan Wallis hands down his report after the inquiry concludes in March.
As the major remaining Victorian regional bank, Bank of Melbourne has been touted as a takeover target for over 12 months.

The latest surge in share price coincides with the conclusion of the New South Wales-based St George Bank /Advance Bank merger and follows the creation late last year of the Queensland mega-bank, combining Metway Bank, Queensland Industry Development Corporation and major insurance player, Suncorp.
The latest round of rumours had provided little new with the focus clearly on the upcoming Wallis report, other said.
"I think it is the same old rumours," said dealer Mark Pervan of Daiwa Securities.
"That sector looks like there will be some kind of takeover activity. I expect a shakeup there and you will probably see some positioning leading up to the Wallis report."
By 2.20 p.m. (0120 GMT), Bank of Melbourne shares had eased from their highs to be up 35 cents on the day at A$8.95 on turnover of 224,008 shares.
